tasks.title: Rust-native release plan: tally campaign release --plan
tasks.goal: Build the release surface the plan's chapter 3 wanted, directly in Rust (its Python lineage was deleted in chapter 2; D34: never build code that is about to die). `tally campaign release <owner/repo> <worklist> --plan` reads durable local state only: the v4 registration (campaign_registry.rs), the attempt-receipts JSONL (attempt-receipts-v1.jsonl under the campaign state), the integration/archive summary refs, the checkpoint refs, and the trailer oracle on merged commits (Tally-Task/Tally-Revision). It renders the release plan: version, ordered conventional-commit release notes derived from the merged task commits, the gate-proof checkpoint ref, and the artifact list. No network, no gh, no writes — plan mode is pure render to stdout as JSON plus human text. Consume the ported folds from tally-core (your dependency).
deliveredBehaviors: A completed campaign renders a full release plan from durable state alone
Plan mode performs zero writes and zero network

acceptanceCriteria.description: The verb exists and renders a plan for a fixture campaign.

tasks.title: Conventional-commit validator and tally lint-history
tasks.goal: The deterministic commit validator (D26: in the renderer, so crates/tally): type enum feat/fix/refactor/docs/build/chore/test/gate, scope vocabulary supplied per invocation, subject case and no trailing period, header <=72, body wrap <=100, blank-line structure, trailer-block well-formedness including one-contiguous-block and hyphenated BREAKING-CHANGE. Expose `tally lint-history <range>` for operator use and wire the same validator into the release plan's note derivation (reject-and-fall-back semantics identical to the narrator seam: a non-conforming commit renders as its template form, never blocks). Include a trailer-block-poisoning negative case.
deliveredBehaviors: lint-history validates a range with per-commit verdicts
The release plan consumes the same validator

tasks.title: Release execution with an injectable forge program and local idempotency
tasks.goal: The execute half of `tally campaign release`: tag, release notes publication, and artifact attachment run through an injectable gh program (a --gh-program flag plus config surface; the old TALLY_GH_PROGRAM precedent was deleted with the forge IO — build the seam fresh and test through a recording shim). Idempotency derives from the LOCAL release record written beside the campaign state (D4: never from public body markers): re-running execute after partial failure skips completed steps by consulting the record, and completes the remainder. The real gh on the operator's PATH is only reached when no shim is injected.
deliveredBehaviors: Execute is resumable from its local release record after any partial failure
All forge writes go through the injectable program; tests use a recording shim

tasks.title: Probe repository lifecycle with a shim-forge lane proof
tasks.goal: The D9 probe: `tally campaign release --probe` exercises the full release act against a disposable target through the injectable program seam. The lane criterion runs entirely against the shim forge (record/replay), proving: probe target naming (tally-probe-*), full plan+execute cycle, teardown, and a written probe receipt. The REAL probe run against GitHub is a named pre-release operator step, not a lane criterion (lanes run forge-less by doctrine). test/release-probe.sh is the operator-facing wrapper you own and create.
deliveredBehaviors: A complete probe cycle runs under the shim forge in-lane
test/release-probe.sh wraps the real operator probe with a receipt

acceptanceCriteria.description: The probe wrapper exists and parses.

tasks.title: Adversarial lane over the release surface
tasks.goal: D71's standing pattern: attack the release surface and fix in place. At minimum: partial-failure injection at every execute step (kill between tag and notes, between notes and artifacts) proving idempotent resumption; malformed durable state (truncated receipts JSONL, missing checkpoint ref) failing loud with named remedies; trailer-oracle poisoning attempts; and the F25 sweep — find any test spawning tally without --config and fix it in place. Fix everything found inside your own domains; report anything out-of-domain as a boundary finding rather than crossing.
deliveredBehaviors: Every injected partial failure resumes correctly
Malformed durable state fails loud with a named remedy
No test spawns tally without --config

This is declaration and enforcement, not restructuring: no storage format changes.

An invariant test enforces derived-only-through-replay

The seam test replays an estate-shaped fixture including legacy gh fields

tasks.title: Reseat the driver suite as the language-agnostic seam harness
tasks.goal: test/spec_build_driver_test.py currently holds 84 tests coupled to Python internals. Reseat it: every test drives the driver ONLY through its public action seam (argv + stdin brief + stdout result + exit code), so the same suite can later run against the Rust driver binary unchanged. A driver-under-test selector (environment variable naming the driver executable, defaulting to drivers/spec_build_driver.py) is the one new mechanism. No test semantics change; count stays within a few of 84 and every retained test passes against the Python driver.
deliveredBehaviors: The suite drives the driver only through the public action seam
A selector chooses the driver executable under test

acceptanceCriteria.description: The reseated suite passes against the Python driver.

tasks.title: The spec-build-driver crate, packaging, and per-action dispatcher
tasks.goal: Create crates/spec-build-driver: a Rust binary with the driver's argv/brief/result contract, initially implementing NO actions itself. Ship the per-action dispatcher: for every action, the Rust binary either handles it natively (none yet) or execs the Python driver (SPEC_BUILD_PY_FALLBACK naming the Python driver path, defaulting to the packaged one) — so the port lands incrementally green, action by action. Package it in the flake (workspace member, tallySource filter if needed) and install it beside the existing driver in libexec; the packaged Python driver stays the default until the seam proof repoints.
deliveredBehaviors: The Rust driver binary dispatches every action, falling back per-action to Python
The flake builds and installs it
